kill_fact: The '14x private-market mark' that anchors the entire sum-of-the-parts is not what the buyer says it paid. The bull derives 14x by annualising Long Ridge's outage-impacted Q1-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $26.4m ($105.6m) against the $1.512bn base price. MARA's own 30 April 2026 announcement states Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA (second-half 2025 basis, reflecting the February 2025 hedge swaps and the June 2025 capacity payments) - i.e. the buyer underwrote roughly 10.5x, not 14x. That number is load-bearing in three places: the consensus_delta pillar ('if a power plant clears fourteen times in a private sale, the terminals and railroads are not worth the mid-single-digit implied multiple'), the 14x rail multiple in sop_breakdown, and the forcing_function's claim that 14x is 'the reference price' for a later Jefferson/Repauno sale. On the file's own stated sensitivity of ~$1.86 per share per turn of rail multiple, re-anchoring the rails to the multiple the buyer actually paid removes roughly $6.50 per share of the $8.29 raw base-case equity value. The asymmetry survives because the rail multiple is independently supported by regional-rail comparables and the Citizens initiation, not by the power-plant mark - but the 'hard third-party mark' argument itself does not survive and should stop being cited as validation of the multiple.
corrections: 1) MULTIPLE (material). Replace '$1.52bn is about fourteen times the plant's annualised Q1 EBITDA of $26.4m' with: the buyer's disclosed underwriting is ~$144m annualised adjusted EBITDA, implying ~10.5x on the $1.512bn base price. The 14x figure annualises a quarter management itself flagged as outage-depressed. Strike the private-mark-validates-the-multiple argument from consensus_delta and from forcing_function; keep the rail multiple only to the extent regional-rail comparables support it. 2) OUTSIDE DATE (material). The dossier states 'neither has published a contractual outside date, so 30 September 2026 is a guided quarter-end rather than a binding deadline.' This is wrong in both directions. The equity purchase agreement signed 29 April 2026 carries a contractual outside date of 30 NOVEMBER 2026, extendable by a further SEVEN MONTHS (to approximately 30 June 2027) if regulatory approvals remain pending and all other conditions are satisfied. The deal is MORE binding than the file credits, and the window is far LONGER than the moderator's 'closes inside the next ten weeks.' The buyer can lawfully wait into mid-2027 while FERC pends - the same period over which the Repauno term loan matures (30 Nov 2026), the Jefferson bridge matures (30 Jun 2027), and operating cash flow stays negative. Catalyst timing risk is understated; deal bindingness is understated too. 3) CONDITIONS LIST (material). 'The conditions list is short: antitrust clearance and a change-of-control approval from FERC' is incomplete. The agreement also requires Surface Transportation Board authorisation under 49 C.F.R. 1180 for the railroad-related asset transactions, absence of a material adverse effect, and third-party consents under material contracts. A three-regulator gate is not a short list. 4) FINANCING / FLOOR (minor, and it cuts FOR the bull). 'No financing contingency has been disclosed' is correct as stated - no financing condition applies to the buyer's obligations - but the agreement contains a $75 MILLION reverse termination fee payable by MARA to the sellers if the agreement terminates in certain instances where the buyer's debt financing is not funded, plus a $20 million escrow. That is roughly $0.63 per share of contractual break compensation in the financing-failure branch only, and it is the ONLY genuinely contractual element of the downside anywhere in this file. Name it, and do NOT generalise it into the regulatory-failure branch, where nothing backstops the price. 5) FINANCING SUBSTANCE (minor). The 'buyer cleared its own financing obstacle in June 2026' claim covers only the noteholder consents on Long Ridge's 8.750% senior secured notes due 2032. MARA's funding still rests on a 364-day senior secured bridge commitment of up to $785 million from Barclays, subject to customary conditions - a short-dated bridge on a bitcoin-mining balance sheet, which is precisely why the $75m reverse termination fee exists. 6) WHAT SURVIVES UNCORRECTED. The catalyst is genuinely live, dated and unfired: the FPA Section 203 joint application was filed 8 May 2026 in docket EC26-92 (accession 20260508-5278, comments due 29 May 2026) and no order granting authorisation has issued as of 27 July 2026. The spread has not closed - the shares are below where they traded at announcement. The file's own correction of the $3.90 'floor' to a behavioural $2.50-$3.00 break price, and its explicit statement that this is a defined-catalyst / undefined-risk position with negative book equity of $303.1m and negative $69.4m operating cash flow, is the honest reading and is confirmed by the Q1 10-Q. The PJM Independent Market Monitor's 29 May 2026 comment seeks CONDITIONS, not denial and not a trial-type hearing, which supports the file's read of it as a delay risk rather than a deal-break risk.
evidence: FTAI Infrastructure Inc. Form 8-K, equity purchase agreement signed 29 April 2026 (announced 30 April 2026): base purchase price $1.512bn with $20m escrowed; closing conditions comprise FERC authorisation under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act, expiration of the HSR waiting period, Surface Transportation Board authorisation under 49 C.F.R. 1180 for railroad-related asset transactions, no material adverse effect, and third-party consents; NO financing condition applies to the buyer's obligations; contractual outside date of 30 November 2026 with a possible seven-month extension if regulatory approvals remain pending; $75m termination fee payable by buyer to sellers in certain instances where the buyer's debt financing is not funded. Directly refutes the file's 'no contractual outside date' and 'conditions list is short: antitrust and FERC'.

MARA Holdings, Inc. press release, 30 April 2026 (ir.mara.com, 'MARA Advances Its Optimized Digital Infrastructure Strategy with Agreement to Acquire Long Ridge Energy & Power'): approximately $1.5bn total transaction value including assumption of at least $785m of debt; Long Ridge contributes approximately $144 million of annualised adjusted EBITDA based on second-half 2025 performance, reflecting the full contractual impact of the February 2025 power hedge swap agreements and the capacity payments commenced June 2025; all-in operating cost under $15/MWh; up to $785m 364-day senior secured bridge loan commitment from Barclays, subject to customary conditions; closing expected in the second half of 2026. Implies ~10.5x on the $1.512bn base price, not the ~14x the bull case annualises off an outage-impacted Q1.

Federal Register, Vol. 91 No. 95, 18 May 2026 (notice 2026-09892), Combined Notice of Filings: Long Ridge Energy Generation LLC and Long Ridge Retail Electric Supplier LLC filed a Joint Application for Authorization Under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act on 8 May 2026, docket EC26-92-000, accession no. 20260508-5278, comment date 5:00 p.m. ET 29 May 2026. No Commission order granting authorisation has issued in that docket as of 27 July 2026 - the catalyst has not fired and the regulatory gate remains genuinely open.

PJM Independent Market Monitor (Monitoring Analytics) comment filed in FERC Docket No. EC26-92, 29 May 2026: urges the Commission to approve the transfer only on condition that MARA commit to keeping Long Ridge's capacity and energy in the PJM markets, and that any new data-centre load be paired with new generation rather than served from the existing plant's output. Relief sought is conditions on approval, not denial and not a trial-type hearing - a delay-and-conditions risk, consistent with the file's characterisation.

FTAI Infrastructure Inc. Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026: total debt $3.84bn; total equity NEGATIVE $303.1m; cash and restricted cash $227.4m; Series B redeemable convertible preferred carried at $152.6m against a $192.0m redemption amount; Series A RailCo preferred (non-controlling) carried at $970.5m against a $1.4bn redemption amount; total revenues $188.4m; net loss $127.2m / $(1.32) diluted EPS; net cash USED in operations $69.4m; $45.9m loss on extinguishment on the replacement $1.35bn term loan at 9.75% due February 2028; liquidity assurance expressly conditioned - management's planned actions 'including the sale of Long Ridge' are considered probable and sufficient to meet obligations over the next twelve months. Confirms there is no asset-backed floor beneath the common.
